text:
Mira (support): FYI — WillowBend reported a sudden p99 jump on embeddings endpoint this morning during their hourly batch. They see 99th go from ~230ms to ~2.1s and some 504s. Sample request ID: req_0a3b9c (they pasted it). They say it started at 07:43 UTC and repeats about every 5m for ~40s. Can we triage?

Vikram (eng-sre): Thanks — do we know which pool they're hitting (shared vs dedicated)? Any tenant-level throttles in place? Could be noisy neighbor from big batch jobs.

Mira (support): They're on hosted shared-default, no dedicated reservation. Customer says the job is a bursty embed batch (100k short texts in spikes). Attached their repro curl and one sample response with long latency.

Mira (support): Repro curl they sent:
```bash
curl -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-compact-1","inputs":["...bulk...","...bulk..."]}' \
  -v
```
(They included request header `x-customer-id: willowbend` in example logs.)

Josh (eng-runtime): If they're sending large synchronous batches we could be hitting queue/backpressure + long kernel scheduling windows. Also continuous-batching can make single-tenant bursts amplify latency for others if not isolated. Need tail traces (rpc spans) and which host group. Can someone pull traces for `req_0a3b9c` and the 07:43-07:50 window?

Vikram (eng-sre): Pulling traces now. Also checking infra metrics for shared-pool-1. Early look: sustained enqueue depth spike on shared-pool-1 at 07:43 and a handful of hosts with CPU pinned at 95%. Looks like a bursty embed job overlapped with normal traffic.

Ran (oncall): I can apply a temporary per-tenant throttle and a short reservation. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Per-tenant throttle to 30 rps (smooth bursts) 2) Create ephemeral reserved capacity binding for 2h to offload heavy flows -> reserve-ephemeral-willow-1 3) Add a short-lived route that sends `x-customer-id: willowbend` to reserved pool. OK to apply?

Mira (support): Customer consented to temporary mitigation (they're scared of 504s). Please proceed — they asked for fastest fix.

Ran (oncall): Applied per-tenant throttle 30rps at 07:55 UTC and created reserve-ephemeral-willow-1 bound to their tenant at 07:57 UTC. Commands used:
```
# apply throttle policy
redwoodctl tenants throttle set --tenant willowbend --rate 30
# create ephemeral reservation
redwoodctl reservations create --name reserve-ephemeral-willow-1 --pool dedicated-spot --duration 2h --tenant willowbend
```

ops-bot: Action taken: throttle_policy=30rps applied to willowbend by Ran; reservation reserve-ephemeral-willow-1 created.

Ran (oncall): Initial impact — p99 dropped from ~2.1s to ~620ms within 2 minutes after reservation routed. No more 504s observed in the window. p95 remained stable. Will monitor for 30m.

Aisha (customer-success): Great. Customer asked about a permanent fix (they want predictable SLAs). I suggested Dedicated and a cost estimate. Can eng-runtime provide a rough cost delta and guidance on how much reserved capacity they'd need for their hourly batch?

Josh (eng-runtime): Quick estimate ask: need their peak concurrent tokens / GPU seconds. If they can share batch size / concurrency we can recommend either steady Dedicated VM (if sustained) or scheduled ephemeral reservations for hourly bursts. For now, we should also offer a bespoke allowlist (burst-reservation allowlist) so that IPs or API keys from WillowBend can be automatically routed to their reservation to avoid manual steps. That requires support ticket + billing approval.

Mira (support): I'll open the allowlist/billing request. Draft note to billing: 
"Customer WillowBend requests programmatic route into ephemeral reservation for burst embedding jobs (daily cadence). Please confirm pricing and be prepared to approve a monthly reserved bucket or a usage-based surcharge for ephemeral reservations."

Vikram (eng-sre): Two follow-ups from infra side: 1) add a short-term autoscaling rule for the ephemeral reservation to avoid under-provisioning mid-burst 2) create an alert for enqueue depth per-pool to detect similar cross-tenant spikes earlier. I can sketch alert thresholds.

Ran (oncall): Will keep monitoring. No regression after 40m check — p99 steady ~550-700ms. If we see repeat after reservation expires, we'll recommend customer schedule an automated reservation or move to Dedicated.

Mira (support): Messaging back to WillowBend: "We applied a temporary throttle and ephemeral reservation which reduced your p99. To avoid recurrence we recommend either scheduled ephemeral reservations for your hourly job or moving to Dedicated. We're submitting an allowlist + billing request to make the routing seamless. Can you run your job now (small window) and paste any request IDs if you still see >1s latency?"

Josh (eng-runtime): Also add a short note for runbook: if p99 spike and enqueue depth spike coincide with tenant burst pattern, prefer ephemeral reservation + throttle before bouncing to customer. Add example commands above and where to check traces.

Mira (support): Customer replied: "Thanks, we ran the job and latencies look normal now. We'll schedule a call to discuss dedicated. Please share estimate."

Aisha (customer-success): I'll coordinate call and get usage details. I'll also ask for their preferred cadence for ephemeral reservations if they don't want Dedicated yet.

Vikram (eng-sre): Filed infra ticket to add enqueue-depth alert and autoscale rule for ephemeral reservations: INFRA-4728. Assigning to @Vikram.

Ran (oncall): Closing short-term action: mitigation in place and effective. Leaving reservation active for 2h (will auto-expire). If anyone needs the raw traces or the request IDs, I saved them under /internal/support/willowbend/1943219999/trace-archive.zip.

Mira (support): Thanks all — I'll mark this thread resolved after Aisha confirms next steps with WillowBend.
